findings.issue: contradicts task clause: "The phase report / status surfaces the count the way other recorded facts are surfaced; ... with no block recorded, say 'not measured', never 'none found'." No status or report surface reads the floor block. The only readers of floor_summary / floor_block / floor_lines are the two reviewer briefs and the one-line `did` text submit prints (grep over plugins/ and tools/). The executor's outcome says NOT DONE and gives the reason (no status or report module is among the task's files, and none shows filed-return facts today). findings.resolution: Either land the surface (have _status_facts.py or the phase report call _filed_returns.floor_summary per filed executor return, so 'not measured' and 'N file(s) not compared' show where other recorded facts show), or record the carve-out as a follow-up task in SG1 with its own tests.add so the clause is not silently dropped at sign-off. findings.issue: Acceptance 4 ('An agent-supplied floor block in the return is not trusted') holds only on the `submit` route. floor_block trusts any block carrying the string mark `source: floor-guard` with well-formed lists, and `submit` is the only place that pops an agent's block. A return filed straight through `audit-task.py file-return` with a typed, marked block is read back by the briefs as the script's reading. `ffg3` only proves an unmarked block is untrusted. The README and execute-task.md say 'an agent's own block is dropped' without that limit. This is the same exposure `helper_red_first` already has for redFirst, which the task said to follow, so it is the module's existing weakness repeated, not a new one.
findings.resolution: Word the README and execute-task.md sentence as 'dropped by `submit`', and state that the mark is a convention rather than a proof. If the class is wanted closed, record it once for redFirst and floorGuard together (for example a digest the verb binds to the return), not for this key alone.

intent.note: Does the diff do what the clauses asked: mostly yes, with one scope difference. Met: submit and the headless writer path (file_writer_return) compute the guard over the task's diff against tree_head(ctx, tree) via task_root, the one base the red helper, stamp and compare read. flr6 holds the base equal to the red helper's throwaway HEAD after HEAD moved. Declared tests.add paths and casesAdded ids are passed by floor_declared. The verb writes the block with source=floor-guard and `submit` pops an agent's block first (flr3/flr4, ffg3). A crash is filed as could-not-tell naming the exception's type and the filing completes (flr5). The brief shows findings, notRead (with move and reason) and couldNotTell as three headings and says NOT clean overall for clean-with-unread, and 'Not measured ... never as a diff with no move in it' with no block (fgb1-fgb6). floorGuard is an object with mode report|off and acceptedSuppressions, handed on as written, in DEFAULTS, the schema, the README table, COMPATIBILITY.md (the promise is narrow, and says a later release may refuse) and the CHANGELOG. The validator reports a wrong shape and the repo's own audit.config.json gains acceptedSuppressions ["noqa: E402"], which the outcome says. The reviewer agent doc gains the input row and one rule line. The file is 7525 bytes now, against the 7532 in the claim; the claim's 6993 under the 7000 ceiling is measure-context's figure, which I did not re-run. Diverges: the clause 'The phase report / status surfaces the count the way other recorded facts are surfaced' is not implemented, and the executor's own note says so (NOT DONE). Under the brief's rule that is `diverges` even though the executor's note agrees with the narrowing. Also verified from the diff: the panel Settings card ('Weakened tests') changes the page the panel digest covers, so the screenshot re-capture was owed, and the orchestrator has done it. Does the claim describe the diff: yes in substance. The claim's gates entry reads 'fail' because sc1/sc2 in tests/test__refs.py were red at filing from the stale screenshot digest. The recorded gate run (2026-11-16T21:55:29Z.3aef45) is passed after the re-capture. The scope additions (_panel_settings.py and tests/test__panel_settings.py) are described accurately and are forced by the vocab-drift and 'Settings binds a control to EVERY key' tests. Known limits stated honestly in the claim: in the phase tree a change already dirty at start is read as the task's, and a tests.add entry with no casesAdded id (always the case for a headless writer) declares its whole file, so a rewritten existing test there lands in `declared` rather than `findings`; the brief still lists `declared` for the reviewer.
